description.summary: forward the current cursor shape to privileged clients

protocol.description:
This protocol forwards the compositor's current cursor shape (as requested by client apps via wp_cursor_shape_v1, or chosen internally by labwc) to a privileged remote-desktop tool. It exists so the remote viewer can render its own cursor with the matching CSS `cursor:` value at zero RTT in position, while the server-side cursor sprite stays hidden (see PORTAL_HIDE_CURSOR).
This is a labwc extension; it is *not* a generalisation of wp_cursor_shape_v1, which is a client-to-compositor request interface. This is a compositor-to-observer event stream.

interface.name: portal_cursor_shape_manager_v1
interface.description: Singleton global. After binding, the compositor emits one `shape` event with the current shape, then continues to emit `shape` on every change.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Releases the manager. Subsequent shape changes are not delivered to this client.

event.name: shape
event.description:
Emitted immediately on bind with the current shape, then on every observed change.
The `shape` argument matches `wp_cursor_shape_device_v1.shape` enum values (1..34 inclusive). Compositor-internal cursors (e.g. resize edges over server-side decorations) are mapped onto the same enum.
Implementations should treat unknown values (outside 1..34) as "default" for forward-compatibility.
